paper.title: Accurate piezoelectric tensor prediction with equivariant attention tensor graph neural network
paper.research_summary: The paper proposes an equivariant attention tensor graph neural network (EATGNN) to predict the full third-rank piezoelectric tensor for both bulk and 2D materials, leveraging irreducible representation decomposition to respect crystal symmetry and rotational equivariance. It validates predictions against DFT-calculated tensors, achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, and uses the model to screen and discover new high-performance piezoelectric candidates, subsequently confirmed by DFPT calculations.

tasks.objective: To accurately predict the complete third-rank piezoelectric tensor for crystalline materials while respecting crystal symmetry and rotational equivariance.
output_goal: full third-rank piezoelectric tensor in Voigt notation (3×6 matrix for bulk, 3×3 for 2D)

evidence.text: Accurate piezoelectric tensor prediction with equivariant attention tensor graph neural network

Here, we propose an equivariant attention tensor graph neural network (EATGNN) that can identify crystal symmetry and remain independent of the reference frame, ultimately enabling the accurate prediction of the complete third-rank piezoelectric tensor.

stages.stage_goal: To remove outliers and enforce consistency between predicted tensors and material crystallographic symmetry.

evidence.text: Due to the presence of a significant number of outliers in the piezoelectric tensors, we performed data resampling before applying machine learning techniques to prevent overfitting.

We first checked whether the piezoelectric tensors in the dataset satisfy the symmetry of their corresponding crystal structures. This was achieved by applying the crystal structure’s symmetry operations to the tensor and checking if it remains invariant under these operations. If a change occurred, we transformed the tensor into a symmetry-compliant form that respects the lattice symmetry22.

stages.stage_goal: To train the equivariant attention tensor graph neural network to predict piezoelectric tensors using symmetry-respecting irreducible representations as targets.

evidence.text: Networks are trained using a mean-squared-error loss function based on complete piezoelectric tensor: loss = 1/N Σ_N n=0 Σ_i,j,k (e′_nijk − e_nijk)² / 27

EATGNN can establish the relationship between crystal structures and their properties. The architecture and speciﬁc details of EATGNN are shown in Fig. 1. It takes the crystal structure as input22, represents it as a crystal graph G(V; E), and utilizes message passing and multi-head attention mechanism to update the graph across multiple graph attention layers. Ultimately, the model outputs the piezoelectric tensor in its irreducible representation...

The training data for the model presented in this work is sourced from Computational 2D Materials Database (C2DB)33,34, the Material Project21 and a recent high-throughput computational study on piezoelectric tensors30.

In order to discover new potential high-performance piezoelectric materials, we use our model on both 3D and 2D materials in the Materials Project and 2DMatPedia database36, respectively. Our selection criteria are 1) out of the training datasets, 2) inversion asymmetry, 3) Egap > 0.1 eV, and 4) Nuc < 30 atoms.
Ultimately, we obtained a dataset comprising 3444 entries, and these data were randomly divided into training and test sets in a 9:1 ratio.

The piezoelectric tensor data of 2D materials was obtained from the C2DB database33,34, comprising a total of 1382 data points, after analyzing and removing some extreme outliers to prevent the model from learning an inaccurate data distribution, 1350 data points were retained and randomly split into training and test sets with 9:1 ratio.
